name: STAR Numerics — real roots of quadratics and cubics
summary: Distinct real roots of quadratics and cubics with the number of roots decided in exact arithmetic and each root isolated by exact-sign bisection, plus Horner evaluation; on 640 polynomials the count equals SymPy's exact count and every root equals the exact root rounded to a float; reproduces the classic cancellation example.
reference: Forsythe, Pitfalls in computation (1970) and Numerical Recipes 5.6: x^2 - 1e8 x + 1 has the roots 1e8 and 1e-8, and the textbook formula loses the small one
reference_observed: quadratic_roots(1, -1e8, 1) = (1e-08, 99999999.99999999): both roots correct to the last digit

na.G-14: no performance requirement declared by any user

review.G-04: coefficients highest power first; roots returned as a sorted tuple of distinct floats
review.G-06: no external data; cross-check corpus generated with a fixed seed
review.G-08: pure functions, standard library only, no IO
review.G-13: ValueError for every invalid input; bisection over the floats ends in at most 64 exact-sign steps; what 'exact' does and does not mean stated
